module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Asymptotics of an inner sum formula for $a(n)$

The inner sum of the formula used in a:
$$\sum_{\max(k-n+5, 0) \le j \le \min(k,4)} \binom{8-j}{j}\binom{2n-k+j-10}{k-j}$$

a: A total of $n$ married couples, including a mathematician M and his wife, are to be seated
at the $2n$ chairs around a circular table, with no man seated next to his wife. After the ladies
are seated at every other chair, M is the first man allowed to choose one of the remaining chairs.
The sequence gives the number of ways of seating the other men, with no man seated next to his
wife, if M chooses the chair that is 9 seats clockwise from his wife's chair.

$$a(n) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } n \le 5 \cr
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k(n-k-1)! \sum_{\max(k-n+5, 0) \le j \le \min(k,4)}
\binom{8-j}{j}\binom{2n-k+j-10}{k-j} & \text{if } n > 5 \end{cases}$$

*References:*
- [A258667](https://oeis.org/A258667)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA258667


open scoped Topology

open BigOperators Nat Int Real Asymptotics Filter

/--
The inner sum of the formula used in a:
$$\sum_{\max(k-n+5, 0) \le j \le \min(k,4)} \binom{8-j}{j}\binom{2n-k+j-10}{k-j}$$
-/
def inner_sum (n k : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  let L : ℕ := max 0 (k + 5 - n)
  let U : ℕ := min k 4
  Finset.sum (Finset.Icc L U) fun j =>
    let term1 := Nat.choose (8 - j) j
    -- The top argument of the second binomial coefficient is written in Nat subtraction form.
    let term2 := Nat.choose (2 * n + j - (k + 10)) (k - j)
    ofNat term1 * ofNat term2

/--
a: A total of $n$ married couples, including a mathematician M and his wife, are to be seated
at the $2n$ chairs around a circular table, with no man seated next to his wife. After the ladies
are seated at every other chair, M is the first man allowed to choose one of the remaining chairs.
The sequence gives the number of ways of seating the other men, with no man seated next to his
wife, if M chooses the chair that is 9 seats clockwise from his wife's chair.

$$a(n) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } n \le 5 \cr
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k(n-k-1)! \sum_{\max(k-n+5, 0) \le j \le \min(k,4)}
\binom{8-j}{j}\binom{2n-k+j-10}{k-j} & \text{if } n > 5 \end{cases}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n ≤ 5 then 0 else
  (Finset.sum (Finset.range n) fun k =>
    let sign : ℤ := if k % 2 = 0 then 1 else -1
    -- Nat.factorial (n - 1 - k) is safe since h implies n > 5 and k < n.
    let fac_term : ℤ := ofNat (Nat.factorial (n - 1 - k))

    sign * fac_term * inner_sum n k
  ).natAbs

noncomputable def natFacToReal (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)

/-- The denominator term $k! (n-1)_k$ represented as a Real number. -/
noncomputable def menageDenomTerm (n k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  let k_fac_R := natFacToReal k
  -- (n-1)_k is the falling factorial. Nat.descFactorial (n-1) k is (n-1)!/(n-1-k)!
  let falling_fac := (Nat.descFactorial (n - 1) k : ℝ)
  k_fac_R * falling_fac

/-- The infinite series part of the asymptotic expansion:
$\sum_{k \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^k}{k!(n-1)_k}$. -/
noncomputable def asymptoticSumPart (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  -- The sum is effectively finite since (n-1)_k is 0 for k >= n.
  Finset.sum (Finset.range n) fun k =>
    if k = 0 then 0
    else
      let denom := menageDenomTerm n k
      -- Denominator is non-zero if n >= 1 and 1 <= k < n.
      if denom = 0 then 0
      else ((-1 : ℝ) ^ k) / denom

/-- The proposed asymptotic expression for a(n). -/
noncomputable def asymptoticTerm (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if n ≤ 2 then 0 -- Avoid division by zero, irrelevant for n -> infinity
  else
    let n_R : ℝ := n
    let n_fac_R := natFacToReal n
    let prefactor : ℝ := exp (-2) * (n_fac_R / (n_R - 2))
    prefactor * (1 + asymptoticSumPart n)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 0 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) \sim e^{-2} \cdot n! / (n-2)$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/258667.wip.lean#L427"]
theorem a_is_equivalent_asymptoticTerm :
    IsEquivalent atTop (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ)) asymptoticTerm := by
    sorry

end OeisA258667

findings.description: The theorem captures only leading-order equivalence, potentially less than the asymptotic expansion originally conjectured on OEIS. Writing G(n) = exp(-2) * n!/(n-2), I proved in scratch Lean, without using the research theorem, that for every f, IsEquivalent atTop f asymptoticTerm ↔ IsEquivalent atTop f G. Indeed, asymptoticSumPart n tends to zero. Consequently none of the displayed correction coefficients is constrained. I also formally checked that f = G satisfies this equivalence but fails even the first-correction requirement: its normalized error after 1 - 1/(n-1), divided by 1/(n-1), tends to 1 rather than 0. An infinite asymptotic expansion normally requires a remainder condition for every fixed truncation order; replacing it with an n-dependent finite sum inside IsEquivalent does not express that. This is questionable rather than a definite misformalization because the current OEIS proof note explicitly adopts the leading-order interpretation.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A258667, Comments (read through https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A258/A258667.seq), first says U_n has the 'asymptotic expansion U_n ~ e^(-2)*n!*(1 + Sum_{k>=1} (-1)^k/(k!(n-1)_k))', then conjectures a(n) ~ e^(-2)*n!/(n-2) times the same infinite series. This suggests an all-orders expansion; the denominators vanish for k ≥ n, so the infinite display is not an ordinary real-valued series. However, Ralf Stephan's June 30, 2026 comment calls the conjecture proved by establishing equivalence to exp(-2)*(n-1)!. The OEIS-linked arXiv:2608.11941, Appendix A, likewise states a finite-sum equivalence. Thus the source's original expansion wording and its later interpretation leave a material ambiguity.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether the intended claim is only leading-order equivalence or a full expansion. If the latter, retain the existing theorem as a leading-order variant and state, for every fixed m : ℕ, that (a(n)/G(n) - ∑_{k=0}^m (-1)^k/menageDenomTerm(n,k)) = o(n^(-m)) as n → ∞. The fixed truncation makes all denominators nonzero eventually. If only leading-order equivalence is intended, explicitly document that the full expansion is not being asserted.

reformulations.difference: Lean applies Int.natAbs to the signed inclusion–exclusion sum, whereas the source presents the signed sum directly as a(n).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Shevelev–Moses equation (5.14), with r = 6 (distance d = 9), identifies exactly this sum with the permanent of a (0,1)-matrix for n > 5. It is therefore nonnegative, so natAbs preserves its value. Both definitions give zero for n ≤ 5. The interval bounds also ensure all binomial arguments and factorial subtractions used by the formula are nonnegative.

review.notes: All declarations were inspected. Lean evaluation reproduced every published term for n = 1 through 24. /workspace/review/scratch.lean checks the small inputs, safe subtraction bounds, empty inner sums, and denominator-zero cases. /workspace/review/asymptotics.lean proves the correction tends to zero, the equivalence with the leading term, and the first-correction counterexample; the named results use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, not sorryAx. The research-solved tag agrees with the current OEIS record, and the OEIS-linked proof targets the same leading-order statement. No separate status issue is reported.
